I bought my first .45 ACP when is was 19 years old. Even back in the days of yore (I am retired now so that gives you an idea I ain't no young duck) the Colt government model were expensive and a farm kid just didn't have the case to plunk down on a Colt. But one day I walked into the local pawn shop and saw a Argentine Model 1927 in .45 auto cal that was dirt cheap. I think it was $69.95 or in that neighborhood. So I bought the thing. I loaded it up with some .45 ACP ammo and it shot pretty well for pitted bore.

Fast forward a few years. I now had some cash and thought I would up grade the old Argentine Model 1927. I bought a Colt national Match barrel and bushing, and a match trigger adjustable for horizontal and vertical rear sight and higher front sight blade.. I got out my files and stones and got to work. Imagine my surprise when I found that the Old Argentine 1927 was a carbon copy down to the smallest pin of the M1911A1. I replaced the barrel and bushing with the national match barrel and bushing. If you decide you want to do this your self be aware there is a lot of fitting that needs to be done. The top tang of the breech must be precisely fitted to the slot in the slide if the barrel is going to lock up properly. Also the ramp at the bottom of the barrel needs to be fitted so that it ramps up properly on the slide stop disassembly pin. The barrel bushing needs to be fitted to the slide. If this is barrel busing is fitted properly on a national match weapon the slide need to be racked back slightly and a busing wrench is need to remove the busing.

I thought about removing the sights from the Argentine slide but decided against it because it was so beautifully blued and the sights were an ugly flat black. Also I wanted to carry the weapon in a holster. So I didn't do anything to the slide. I installed the match trigger, adjusted the trigger pull to 4.5 lbs and took it to the range. Once I got through with all the mods I found that I could shoot sub 3 inch groups at 25 yds. with factory ammo. I currently own four .45 cal pistols (1 Colt gold cup, 1 EAA witness, 1 Sig Saur P227 and my Argentine model 27) and i like my argentine Model 27 best of all.

Thanks for sharing. I've looked at many of these over the years, but have never run across the 'deal' I wanted at the moment. But being a C&R collector, I know them well, and also know they're well made and liked. I actually search gunbroker often, looking for just the right one, and one day may jump in. Definitely a nice handgun.
